theory.intro: Use a number line. The first number is where you start; the second tells you how far to move.
steps: Start at the first integer on the number line.
Add → move right by the second number.
Subtract → move left by the second number.
Read off where you land (you may pass zero).
For more than one operation, continue from the last answer and work from left to right.

workedExamples.question_text:
Use a number line to evaluate each expression.
a) $-7 + 4$
b) $-7 - 4$
c) $-8 + 8$
Use a number line to evaluate $6 - 9 + 5$.

The temperature is $5^\circ\mathrm{C}$. It falls by $8$ degrees.
What is the new temperature?
workedExamples.solution_text:
A fall of $8$ degrees means subtract $8$.
Start at $5$ and move $8$ units left.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}5-8\\&=-3\end{aligned}$
The new temperature is $-3^\circ\mathrm{C}$.
